metaData.originalTitle: AI 商业化的十字路口：为什么广告与订阅都难以单独走通？
metaData.title: The Crossroads of AI Commercialization: Why Advertising and Subscriptions Alone Are Both Unsustainable
metaData.oneSentenceSummary: This article delves into the structural ceilings faced by AI's two mainstream monetization models—advertising and subscriptions—and argues that the true long-term opportunity lies in shifting from a 'traffic logic' to a 'task logic,' and from an 'attention economy' to an 'execution economy.'
metaData.summary: Using the commercialization paths of OpenAI and Anthropic as comparative examples, the article systematically analyzes the fundamental contradictions AI faces in monetization. It points out that the advertising model is constrained by the low proportion of commercializable queries in AI conversations (only 1/5 to 1/4 of traditional search), the limited number of ads that can be embedded in a single response (only 1/3 to 1/2 of traditional search), and an invisible ceiling of user trust. The subscription model, on the other hand, grapples with a cost structure dilemma: the marginal cost of AI inference is non-zero and non-negligible, leading to structural losses under a 'low-price subscription + heavy user' model in the Agent era. The article argues that the future of AI commercialization is not a binary choice between 'subscription or advertising,' but rather a shift from 'selling access' to 'selling outcomes.' This involves building business models around deep services such as enterprise workflows, platform-level services, and transaction commissions. It concludes that as Agents begin to complete tasks for users, the value of AI will shift from 'what was answered' to 'what was accomplished.'

mainPoints.point: The AI advertising model faces three structural ceilings: a low proportion of commercializable queries, limited ad load capacity, and user trust risks.
mainPoints.explanation: Compared to traditional search, the proportion of queries with clear commercial intent in AI conversations is extremely low. Furthermore, it is difficult to embed multiple ads in a single AI response, and users demand higher trust from the AI's 'assistant' role, where excessive ad integration undermines neutrality.

mainPoints.point: The core contradiction of the AI subscription model lies in non-zero marginal costs, leading to structural losses under a 'low-price subscription + heavy user' model in the Agent era.
mainPoints.explanation: Unlike traditional software and SaaS, large model inference incurs ongoing token costs, with complex tasks potentially consuming several dollars in compute. This makes it difficult for platforms to balance pricing, usage limits, and user experience.

mainPoints.point: The future of AI commercialization lies in shifting from 'traffic logic' to 'task logic,' and from an 'attention economy' to an 'execution economy.'
mainPoints.explanation: Users are willing to pay for 'task outcomes,' and merchants are willing to pay for more deterministic leads and transactions. Therefore, the long-term opportunity lies in deep services like enterprise workflows, platform-level services, and transaction commissions, rather than pure advertising or subscriptions.

keyQuotes: The crossroads of AI commercialization is essentially not a binary choice between 'subscription or advertising,' but a process where the AI industry shifts from traffic logic to task logic, and from an attention economy to an execution economy.
When Agents start doing things for users, the value of AI will also shift from 'what was answered' to 'what was accomplished.'
The stronger the AI, the longer the context, the more complex the tool calls, the longer the task chain, and the higher the inference consumption it often entails.
Users may not be willing to pay for a single Q&A, but they are willing to pay for a successful travel plan, a cheaper insurance plan, or a more effective resume optimization.

relatedArticles.title: Where is Education Headed in the Age of AI?
relatedArticles.oneSentenceSummary: This article deeply explores the reconstruction of the underlying logic of education in the AI era, pointing out that the focus of education should shift from standardized knowledge transfer to cultivating core competencies that AI cannot replace, such as problem definition, cross-domain integration, and intrinsic motivation.

relatedArticles.title: Seven Questions on Tokenomics: An Introductory Map to the New AI Economy
relatedArticles.oneSentenceSummary: This article systematically elaborates on the economic logic of Tokens as the core unit of measurement in the AI era, covering industrial background, value stratification, cost evolution, and future trends driven by autonomous agents.

relatedArticles.title: Understanding Harness Engineering: Finding the Shell That Keeps AI from Going Rogue—Insights from 14 Engineering Articles | Hao's Trend Talk
relatedArticles.oneSentenceSummary: This article provides an in-depth analysis of "Harness Engineering," a core technology in the AI Agent field. It reveals how to compensate for model shortcomings through a three-layer management architecture and proposes the logic of "Compensation Surface Migration" that evolves with model capabilities.

relatedArticles.title: Vol.89 AI Industry 2025 Annual Summary Supplement (V4 "Can't Wait" Edition) --- 70-page PPT Solo
relatedArticles.oneSentenceSummary: A panoramic review of the AI industry dynamics in China and the US in early 2025, deeply deconstructing capital expenditures, the explosion of Agent technology, and AI's impact on the software industry.

relatedArticles.title: GPT-5.4: Professional Workflows Enter the 'Executable Era'
relatedArticles.oneSentenceSummary: GPT-5.4 marks the leap from conversational assistants to autonomous execution agents, deeply embedding into professional workflows through native computer use, dynamic tool search, and interactive thinking.

relatedArticles.title: GPT-5.4 Released: OpenAI's First Unified Model, Truly Native
relatedArticles.oneSentenceSummary: OpenAI releases GPT-5.4, creating the first unified Agent model that supports native Computer Use by integrating reasoning, coding, and computer interaction.

relatedArticles.title: 140. A 4-Hour Interview with Yao Shunyu: Let Me Be a Little Crazy! Training Models at Anthropic and Gemini, Tech Predictions, and the End of Heroism
relatedArticles.oneSentenceSummary: An in-depth conversation with former Anthropic and Google DeepMind researcher Yao Shunyu, sharing frontline experience training Claude 3.7/4.5 and Gemini 3, exploring that model capabilities have not plateaued, the arrival of the AI collectivism era, and the true driving forces behind technological development.

relatedArticles.title: After Large Models: Rewriting the Division of Labor Between Humans and Machines | A 10,000-Word Roundtable Transcript
relatedArticles.oneSentenceSummary: Through a roundtable dialogue between sci-fi writer Chen Qiufan and prompt engineering expert Li Jigang, this article deeply explores the reconstruction of human-machine division of labor in the era of large models: AI eliminates time barriers and takes over techniques, while humans must focus on ideas, taste, and intuition.

relatedArticles.title: When AI Makes Productivity No Longer the Bottleneck, What's Next? | AI Transition Survey 02 - flomo's Shaonan
relatedArticles.oneSentenceSummary: This article features an in-depth conversation with Shaonan, co-founder of flomo, exploring the new bottlenecks teams face when AI contributes 70% of the code: lagging user value discovery, difficulties in restructuring collaboration, and how to redefine 'friction' and the value of note-taking in the AI era.

relatedArticles.title: The Era of Traffic 2.0
relatedArticles.oneSentenceSummary: This article systematically discusses the paradigm shift of internet traffic from the 1.0 model centered on user attention to the 2.0 model centered on agent behavior and token consumption, and analyzes the profound impact of this transformation on various segments of the consumer internet and industry chain participants.
